page.overview:
What is Nug and Yeb?

Nug and Yeb are twin Great Old Ones from the Cthulhu Mythos, who were first mentioned in the short story "The Last Test" by H. P. Lovecraft.

Nug and Yeb were born from the mating of Shub-Niggurath with Yog-Sothoth (: Selected Letters 5.875) and T’yog believed them to be friendly to man. (: "Out of the Aeons")

According to another account by Eibon, the androgynous Cxaxukluth split in two, becoming male Nug and female Yeb. This minority interpretation may just be a textual gloss attempting to harmonize conflicting information. (: "The Second Epistle of Eibon unto his Disciples, or The Apocalypse of Eibon" [Robert M. Price and Laurence J. Cornford])

Nug is the parent of Cthulhu and Yeb is the parent of Tsathoggua (: Selected Letters 4.617). Nug might be known by the name Ptmâk in Hyperborea, as Ptmâk corresponds to the "immediate" parent of Cthulhu. (: letter of Clark Ashton Smith to R. H. Barlow, September 10th, 1935)
